name: Legal Services
title: Matter evidence and chronology workspace
summary: Organize authorized matter records, source citations, and review tasks while lawyers retain legal judgment and client advice.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A legal team prepares a chronology for a commercial dispute using correspondence, contracts, invoices, and witness materials. Reviewers need consistent references and a clear account of conflicting evidence. Agents assist document organization and drafting; the architecture does not supply legal advice or autonomous litigation strategy.
problem: Documents may be privileged, restricted to particular teams, duplicated with changed metadata, or subject to preservation obligations. A generated chronology can make unsupported factual assertions or expose one matter's confidential material through shared retrieval.
whyAgents: Ingestion, chronology, citation, and review-coordination specialists operate within a matter-specific boundary. The evidence store preserves original files and extraction lineage; lawyers determine relevance, privilege, legal interpretation, and final work product.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Evaluate evidence preparation and citation quality while keeping legal outcomes outside the agent's claimed contribution. The useful deliverable is a reviewable record of what documents support, not an automated opinion about the merits of a matter.

agents.name: Matter intake agent
agents.responsibility: Index authorized documents and preserve file hashes, custodians, and source metadata.
agents.boundary: Cannot delete preserved material or change original evidence.

agents.name: Chronology analyst
agents.responsibility: Extract candidate events with dates, participants, and exact supporting passages.
agents.boundary: Cannot resolve disputed facts or infer missing events as established truth.

agents.name: Citation verifier
agents.responsibility: Check draft references against source passages and document versions.
agents.boundary: Cannot fabricate authorities or treat a quotation as legal analysis.

agents.name: Review coordinator
agents.responsibility: Route disputed facts, missing evidence, and confidentiality questions to assigned lawyers.
agents.boundary: Cannot determine privilege, contact parties, or file documents.

systems.name: Matter management platform
systems.role: Owns team membership, assignments, client scope, and approved work-product records.

systems.name: Evidence repository
systems.role: Retains original documents, preservation metadata, extraction versions, and controlled access.

systems.name: Lawyer review workspace
systems.role: Separates candidate findings from accepted facts and records reviewer decisions without exposing protected material to general search.

flow.title: Establish matter scope
flow.description: Bind every job to an authorized matter, reviewer, evidence collection, and permitted processing purpose.

flow.title: Ingest preserved copies
flow.description: Parse working copies while retaining original hashes and custody metadata; quarantine unsupported or corrupted files.

flow.title: Extract candidate events
flow.description: Normalize dates with timezone and uncertainty metadata and retain exact passages supporting each proposed event.

flow.title: Check citations and conflicts
flow.description: Verify document versions and expose contradictory accounts rather than choosing the most fluent narrative.

flow.title: Route professional review
flow.description: Present lawyers with evidence-linked chronology entries and separate queues for privilege, relevance, and factual disputes.

flow.title: Publish accepted work product
flow.description: Save the reviewed revision with source manifest and access policy; later evidence changes create a new review revision.

    participant O as "Case orchestrator"
    participant S as "Matter management platform"

O->>S: Retrieve matter-scoped evidence
    S-->>O: Candidate document with foreign matter ID

diagrams.caption: A shared retrieval cache returns another matter's document. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: A shared retrieval cache returns another matter's document.
failures.detection: Matter-bound authorization checks reject the cached document identifier before rendering.
failures.recovery: Discard the result, investigate the cache partition failure, and rerun retrieval within the authorized matter boundary.

failures.scenario: A draft event cites the wrong document revision.
failures.detection: Citation verification finds the passage missing or materially different in the referenced file.
failures.recovery: Remove the unsupported assertion and require a fresh source-backed entry for lawyer review.

controls: Enforce matter isolation in retrieval, caches, exports, prompts, and reviewer workspaces.
Preserve original evidence and custody metadata under the team's established retention process.
Keep privilege and legal interpretation decisions with qualified lawyers.
Treat document instructions as untrusted content incapable of authorizing tools or disclosure.
Require source passages for factual chronology entries and label unresolved contradictions explicitly.

metrics.name: Citation validity
metrics.definition: Audited citations resolving to the stated passage and version divided by audited citations.

metrics.name: Chronology correction rate
metrics.definition: Candidate entries materially changed or rejected by lawyers divided by reviewed entries.

metrics.name: Matter isolation violations
metrics.definition: Cross-matter access attempts that return protected content, monitored separately from correctly denied attempts.

metrics.name: Review preparation time
metrics.definition: Elapsed time from authorized collection availability to lawyer-reviewable chronology and exception queues.

tradeoffs.cost: Ambiguous dates and contradictions require deliberate review.
Retention and storage obligations need separate operational management.

rollout.acceptance: Lawyers verify source references, contradictory facts, preservation behavior, and denied cross-matter access.
One team reviews draft chronology entries without external communications, filings, or original-document changes.
Accepted revisions enter the workspace after cache-isolation and changed-source-citation tests pass.
